reading.body:
CyrusOne Florence publishes 5 MW of IT capacity, making it Kentucky's largest disclosed facility, though this remains modest against frontier AI training power budgets.

Kentucky holds three published capacity declarations across five mapped sites totaling 9.55 MW. CyrusOne Florence accounts for more than half that disclosed total. The facility spans 143,000 square feet. At 40 kW per rack, this IT load is roughly 125 racks; at 300 kW per modern accelerator pod, roughly 17 pods. The facility holds PCI DSS, HIPAA, ISO 27001, FISMA, SSAE 16 Type II, and Green Globes certifications, indicating readiness for regulated and security-sensitive tenants.

The 5 MW figure is well below the per-facility capacity of large cloud platforms and does not approach single-site power budgets now consumed by frontier model training. Most data center capacity in Kentucky remains unpublished, so the state's true computational footprint is unknown. The operator's published specifications do not include applied power draw, utilization rate, power purchase agreements, or grid interconnection details.

Whether this site matters to AI scaling depends on tenant workload, grid headroom, and power availability that are not disclosed. The infrastructure exists. The binding constraints remain opaque.
